pageCache.pageTitle: Vision & Values | Prince of Wales Primary School - Enfield
pageCache.text:
Vision & Values
Our current Vision and Values were created collaboratively with all members of our school community. They encompass who we are as a school community, what we believe and what we do as a result.
Our LEARNERS values permeate through our day-to-day learning, language and culture. To help us better understand these, we are helped by our LEARNERS Ambassadors: Lennie Leadership, Erin Explore, Angelica Appreciation, Rahaan Resilience, Noah Nurture, Ethan Enthusiasm, Reyha Reflection and Sonia Sustainability & Stewardship.
To develop our pupils’ sense of belonging, self and place in the community, we ensure we all understand the British Values and Protected Characteristics, and how they relate to us all.

pageCache.pageTitle: Awards & Partners | Prince of Wales Primary School - Enfield
pageCache.text:
Awards & Partners
Our partnerships with the local authority, Haringey Education Partnership (HEP), Enfield Town Schools Partnership (ETSP), as well as engagement with the local community and families through Parent Cafés and study support activities, contribute to a dynamic and engaging learning environment and emphasise our commitment to lifelong learning and community support.
We take pride in our commitment to environmental sustainability. From our RHS 5-star gardening school and Enfield in Bloom Gold awards to our Schools Climate Action Network participation, we actively contribute to creating a greener and healthier world. The installation of solar panels is a testament to our dedication to reducing our carbon footprint.
We have been winners every year since 2010

pageCache.pageTitle: Personal Development | Prince of Wales Primary School - Enfield
pageCache.text:
Personal Development
At Prince of Wales Primary School, we prioritise the personal development of every member of our school community, fostering a culture where everyone is guided by our core values—Leadership, Explore, Appreciation, Resilience, Nurture, Enthusiasm, Reflection, Sustainability and Stewardship. We create an inclusive and nurturing environment that promotes pupils’ spiritual, moral, social, and cultural growth. We are ambitious not only for the progress pupils make during their time with us but also in preparing them thoroughly for their next educational steps, ensuring they develop the knowledge, skills and character needed for lifelong success. Our commitment to personal development embeds equality, respect, and active citizenship.
Throughout the year every pupil experiences a range of educational experiences beyond the classroom, which can be seen in the newsletters each week.

pageCache.pageTitle: Parents | Prince of Wales Primary School - Enfield
pageCache.text:
Parents
At Prince of Wales Primary School, we believe that strong partnerships with parents and carers are essential to the success and well-being of our pupils. We work closely with families to ensure open, honest and supportive communication, creating a collaborative environment where everyone’s voice is valued. Through regular updates, parent workshops and involvement in school events, we keep parents informed and engaged in their child’s learning journey. We also provide tailored support to meet the diverse needs of our community, ensuring all families feel welcomed and empowered to contribute to their child’s personal and academic development. Together, we nurture confident, resilient learners who thrive both in school and beyond.

pageCache.text:
Governing Body
Message from the Chair of Governors – Laraine Hodgson
It is an honour and privilege to have been elected as Chair of Governors at Prince of Wales.
It has always been my belief that if children are happy then they will learn. To that end, I believe that it is vital for home and school work in partnership to ensure the children try their best to achieve, and become the best that they can be through their thirst and eagerness for learning. Successful learning raises standards but not without the hard work of a committed whole staff team who provide a vibrant, rich and diverse curriculum at Prince of Wales. There is nothing more exciting than seeing those awe and wonder moments in children’s learning, and listening to them sharing their learning achievements with those who will listen.
It is important for Governors to know and understand the school, and through meetings and visits we work hard to provide the best support we can as ‘critical friends’, as the school continues to move forward on its ever improving journey.

pageCache.pageTitle: Attendance | Prince of Wales Primary School - Enfield
pageCache.text:
Attendance
We recognise that consistent attendance significantly enhances children’s academic achievements and overall development. Therefore, we are committed to ensuring that students attend school daily and arrive on time.
Regular attendance and good punctuality can:
Reporting Your Child’s Absence
If your child is too unwell to attend school or has a medical appointment, please notify the School Office on the first day of absence, before 8:30 am.
EMAIL: office@princeofwales.enfield.sch.uk
Our attendance officer monitors pupil absences daily, and we collaborate closely with Enfield Local Education Authority to maintain high attendance rates.
Please be advised that;
In accordance with school policy, permission for absences due to holidays during term time will not be granted.
Attending a medical or dental appointment during the school day will not be authorised, unless it is a specialist hospital appointment, that cannot happen outside of the school day. Medical evidence, e.g. hospital letter, would be required.
Punctuality is also important; children are expected to arrive at school on time. We have a strict monitoring system in place for pupils who arrive after 8:45 am. Additionally, please ensure your child is collected promptly at the end of the school day, as late pick-ups can be distressing for children. If you are delayed for any reason, kindly contact the school as soon as possible to inform us of the situation.
Let’s work together to achieve the highest possible attendance and punctuality at Prince of Wales. There are 190 school days per year—let’s make them count!

pageCache.pageTitle: Pupil Premium | Prince of Wales Primary School - Enfield
pageCache.text:
Pupil Premium
Pupil Premium Strategy Report
Pupil Premium Report Pupil Premium Report with Year 3 Evaluation
UNIVERSAL INFANT FREE SCHOOL MEALS AND FREE SCHOOL MEALS – THE DIFFERENCE
UIFSM is not to be confused with being eligible for FSM. UIFSM is offered to all Key stage 1 children until they join KS2 in year 3. FSM eligibility is an additional entitlement for those children whose parents receive certain benefits. This entitlement can run throughout your child’s time in school and not just in Key stage 1. You may be eligible if you are in receipt of certain benefits and it is worthwhile if you apply as it could mean additional funding for the school to support your child even if they receive a free meal as they are in KS1.
When your child is on the FSM register, the school is given extra funding, and this is called pupil premium. Pupil premium can be used by the school in a variety of ways to help support your child, and this can extend to the school funding ‘extras’ such as your child’s music or dance lessons.
In addition even if pupils lose FSM eligibility, they will remain eligible for the pupil premium for six years after this point, which means your child continues to benefit from some additional funding via pupil premium even when the go to secondary school.
If your child is in year 2 or below, you are in receipt of certain benefits and you have not applied for FSM please ask at the school office for a form to complete which just needs a few simple questions to be answered. A member of the office staff will be happy to help you.

pageCache.pageTitle: School meals | Prince of Wales Primary School - Enfield
pageCache.text:
School meals
Meals are carefully prepared in the school kitchen by a dedicated team to ensure that pupils are offered nutritious and well-balanced lunches including vegetarian and cultural dietary choices.
Our school meals are provided by STIR Home – Stir Food
There are three lunchtime options:
Children may have a cooked school meal;
Menu
Lunch menu until February 25 Half term
Lunch menu after February 25 Half term
Ordering School Lunches
All school lunches must be ordered and paid for in advance. Parents/carers will need to log on to parentpay.com and order their child’s meals, making a selection from the menu, up to two weeks in advance, or before 8am on the day of the lunch. To make selection easier, there is an image of the meal as well. If your child is absent from school, you can cancel any of your pre-ordered meals before 8am on the day.
By involving you in your child’s meal ordering process, it not only helps you ensure your child enjoys a variety of healthy foods but helps us to reduce food wastage too.
You will still be able to pay for your child’s meals at a PayPoint if you prefer to do so, but you must set up and use your online account to order the meals. This system will only allow you to order meals for your child if you have sufficient credit on their account, so please keep this in mind.
If you do not already have a ParentPay account, in order to set it up, you will need an activation letter. This will be provided to you by the school.
I have provided a step by step guide on how to order your child’s meals with this letter.
For further information on ParentPay please visit ParentPay.com. If you need any further assistance or have any questions, please contact the school office.
Online Menu Choice Selection
Packed Lunches
Packed lunches should be sent to school in a suitable named container. Drinks should be in an unbreakable named container. It is expected that packed lunches are nutritious and part of a balanced diet. It is preferred that children do not have sweets in their lunch boxes and there should be not products containing nuts in any part of their lunch. They may also bring in a piece of fruit for break time, however children in Foundation stage and KS1 will be given a piece each day. Please don’t bring food from fast food restaurants as staff will not be able to give that to your child. Children will be asked to keep unopened or unfinished food to return home.
Universal Free School Meals
If your child is in Reception, Year 1 or Year 2 they will be able to receive a school meal at no cost to the parent or guardian. Choosing a school meal will help you save on average £475 per year. Your child may still bring in a packed lunch from home if they prefer. Please note, a cash alternative is not available for those children not taking a school lunch.
Whether or not your child receives a free school meal, it is still really important that you still complete the form to register if they are in Reception, Year 1 or Year 2-this will mean the school receives extra funding for your child’s education.
Free School Meals
If your family receives certain benefits or is on low income you could be eligible for free school meals for your older child/children. It costs nothing to apply but could save you money and the school receives extra funding for your child’s education. To find out if you qualify and how to apply either:
Mayor of London Free Meals for Years 3 to 6
From September 2023, all state primary school children in years 3 to 6 in London are also eligible for free school meals. This initially one year initiative was introduced to tackle the cost-of-living crisis and ensure that all children can enjoy a free lunch for this whole academic year. For our families that could be saving of £475 per child. It is still important that parents register for free meals which entitles the school to receive important funding to support your child’s education.
All Other School Meals
Breakfast is £15.00 for the week – £3.00 per day, minimum payment of £6.00 . Breakfast Club opens at 7:30am
We are a cashless school and payments can be made either online through the ParentPay website or at a Paypoint. Meals should be paid for in advance.

pageCache.text:
Our Curriculum
Curriculum Drivers
Our drivers are an extension of our Vision and values. They drive and shape the foundations of our curriculum and are embedded throughout our subject intents and school culture.
LEARNERS values
Communication and vocabulary
Community and citizenship
Health and Well-being
LEARNERS values
At POW, we foster a love for learning and develop children who are self-motivated by the intrinsic desire to learn and grow. Our values are threaded throughout the school culture, language and curriculum. They form the basis of our interactions, day to day decisions and our high aspirations for all who attend. We encourage all in our community to grow and develop and celebrate the learning journey. Our values provide us with a shared vision and language. Further links to the British values are made throughout our cycle of assemblies and curriculum as appropriate.
Communication and vocabulary
At POW, we believe language is a tool that unlocks opportunities. Our children learn to express themselves accurately, thoroughly and sensitively in order to communicate effectively with the world around them. We value and develop high-quality language and communication skills through our curriculum, a vocabulary-rich environment and quality interactions. Our children have opportunities to develop and articulate their beliefs and opinions in a variety of ways.
Community and citizenship
At POW, within our supportive and diverse community, our children form positive relationships and develop of a sense of self. Our children are empowered by seeing themselves reflected in our curriculum and we celebrate the value of parent/family participation through cafes, forums and cultural events. We create an awareness of our place in the global community and nurture children who are prepared to problem solve when faced with the challenges of tomorrow.We teach them to care for the environment and consider how they can be responsible, make informed choices and be active citizens, who one day will become confident agents of change.
Health and Well-being
At POW, we actively seek opportunities to foster healthy lifestyles and instil positive attitudes in our children through our comprehensive curriculum and enrichment opportunities. By equipping them with this knowledge, we empower our pupils to make informed decisions that contribute to their overall health and future wellbeing, emphasising the current and long-term impact of their decisions. Our extensive grounds provide further opportunities to explore outdoor learning, including learning about growing and harvesting food. We promote positive well-being for all in our school community.

Year 1 Phonics Screening Check
The phonics screening check is a short, light-touch assessment to confirm whether individual children have learnt phonic decoding to an appropriate standard. It will identify the children who need extra help so they are given support by their school to improve their reading skills.

End of Key Stage 1 SATs
At the end of Key Stage 1, teachers use teacher assessment judgements to report on the progress of their pupils. These assessment judgements take into account a pupil’s performance in national curriculum tests (often referred to as SATs) in mathematics, English reading and English grammar, punctuation and spelling. Writing results are solely based on teachers’ assessments of pupils’ writing over time.
End of Key Stage 2 SATs
The National expectation for children at the end of Year 6 is to achieve a scaled score of 100 or more. Currently, there is no National measure for pupils working at greater depth in Reading, Mathematics and SPAG; in the table below, pupils achieving a scaled score of over 108 have been considered to be working ‘at greater depth’.

Financial Information and Benchmarking
The consistent financial reporting (CFR) framework applies to maintained schools and pupil referral units. It’s optional for nurseries and non-maintained special schools.
It provides a standard template to enable our school to collect information about our income and expenditure for each financial year.
The information supports benchmarking and enables our Governors and the Local Authority to produce simple reports. A link to our latest benchmarking data can be found on the link below.
https://financial-benchmarking-and-insights-tool.education.gov.uk/school/102002
Prince Of Wales Primary School is required to publish information regarding any staff who are earning over £100,000 per year. At Prince of Wales Primary School, one member of staff earns over this threshold.
